messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: streaming-p95/p99-surge detected on redwood-runtime-prod-1. p99 12:02:14 -> 1.9s (SLO 1.0s). Affected route: /v1/stream/chat. Autoscale healthy.

alex (oncall): I'm on it. noticing spikes correlated with GPU node 'g-node-47' CPU offload rates rising.

maria (eng-runtime): seeing repeated 'kv-cache miss' + backend stalls in the tail logs. streaming tasks piling up. attaching sample tail: 
```
[2025-11-03T12:02:13Z] stream/req=abc123 p99=1.92s status=200 backend_wait=1.1s gpu_sched=0.6s kv_miss=true ecc_correctables=3
[2025-11-03T12:02:14Z] stream/req=def456 p99=2.10s status=200 backend_wait=1.3s gpu_sched=0.9s thermal_throttle=true
```

jordan (sre): ops metrics show correctable ECC events on g-node-47 increased at 12:00. temp spiked to 84C then throttle events. p95 steady, p99 tail huge.

lee (infra): yep, GPU telemetry: ECC corrected counts rising, GPU frequency dropping due to thermal throttle. looks flaky, maybe fan curve or airflow.

alex (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) drain g-node-47 from serving pool, 2) enable model-fallback-policy (smaller model / quantized) for streaming route, 3) increase CPU fallback workers to handle burst. Doing step 1 now.

alex (oncall): `kubectl cordon g-node-47 && kubectl drain g-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

ops-bot: Drain initiated for g-node-47 by alex. Pods being rescheduled. Estimated 45s.

sam (support): FYI: we have two active customer sessions reporting slow streaming (cust-842 / cust-219). opening priority support cases and adding status note.

maria (eng-runtime): rolling a dynamic Canary: reduce batch_size for /v1/stream/chat from 8->4 and force continuous-kv-cache for prefix matches to reduce backend_wait. Pushing config now.

jordan (sre): scaling note: autoscaler picked new nodes but scheduling hit a limit on allowed GPU instance quota in eu-west-1 region. reschedule to other pool. manually spinning replacement GPU instance now.

lee (infra): spinning hot-swap node in us-west-2 as warm replacement. also raising fan curve on adjacent racks.

alex (oncall): customer impact: p99 for streaming rose to ~2.1s peak for ~6 minutes before mitigations. Affected ~0.7% of requests. No data loss. Filing incident severity: Sev2 for now.

maria (eng-runtime): logs show fallback helped reduce backend_wait to ~0.4s for rerouted traffic. streaming stalls reduced; p99 trending down.

jordan (sre): ECC counts on g-node-47: corrected_count=128 over 10m. suggests hardware flake vs memory instability. I'll tag the node out of rotation and schedule postmortem.

alex (oncall): handoff: I need to hand to lee for hardware remediation + replacement, and maria for runtime root-cause and configuration follow-up. Next on-call in 30m is lee. I'm handing off operational control.

lee (infra): taking ownership for hardware. immediate actions: 1) run `nvidia-smi -q` and `dmesg | grep -i ecc`, 2) order physical inspection if corrected errors persist after a reboot, 3) plan cold-swap if needed.

maria (eng-runtime): I'll open an evaluation ticket to test if prefix KV caching + smaller batch is safe for QoE across our eval prompts. also add regression alert on p99 for streaming route.

sam (support): Posted status update to customers in status.redwood.com (incidents/2512345678). Notified cust-842 and cust-219 with temporary mitigations and ETA for full resolution.

alex (oncall): summary for handoff:
- root symptom: GPU node degradation causing thermal throttling + ECC correctable surge -> increased backend_wait and streaming tail.
- mitigations executed: drained node, enabled fallback model variant, reduced batch size, increased CPU fallback workers, spun a replacement warm node, updated fan curve.
- current state: p99 back to ~0.98s, p95 stable. autoscaler completed replacement in non-quota region.
- action items: lee to validate hardware and RMA if needed; maria to run regression/eval and make fallback config persistent; jordan to write incident timeline and attach GPU telemetry.

lee (infra): running quick checks now. `nvidia-smi -q` shows ECC errors persisted after drain. will try controlled reboot once traffic is fully moved.

ops-bot: Replacement node g-node-92 joined pool at 12:06:52. Traffic shifting.

maria (eng-runtime): recommending we add automatic fallback threshold when corrected_ecc_rate > 10/min or thermal_throttle events > 2 in 5m to preempt SLO breach. opening RFC.

jordan (sre): I'll start the incident timeline doc and assign owners. alex, please add any observed customer-call transcripts or timestamps.

alex (oncall): adding notes to the doc, handing off. I'll be available on pager if needed. :white_check_mark: 

lee (infra): accepted handoff. ETA full hardware verification + RMA decision in 90m.

sam (support): leaving pinned updates in the status page and will notify customers once hardware decision is made.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated (tail latency reduced). handoff: lee (infra) + maria (eng-runtime). Severity maintained at Sev2.

alex (oncall): closing my active oncall window for this incident, leaving timeline draft in #incidents-docs.

lee (infra): final note before root-cause: thermal profile + dust buildup on the rack was likely contributing. will include photos + telemetry in postmortem.

maria (eng-runtime): will follow up with a retro on the fallback thresholds and ensure unit tests cover streaming regressions.

jordan (sre): timeline saved. tagging postmortem and linking support tickets.

ops-bot: Incident thread archived to incidents/2512345678 on request by alex.
